n0.speaker: Dolores
n0.text: Vernon. Your Dedication Hour tonight. Do play something uplifting. The last few have been so... damp.
n0.aside: She is arranging chrysanthemums with the grim precision of a person disarming something.

choices.text: "Dolores, there's a hymn missing from your hymnal. 212."

n1.speaker: Dolores
n1.text: There was never a Hymn 212. The hymnal goes from 211 to 213. That's what a hymnal is, Vernon. A list in order.
n1.aside: Her hand has stopped on a chrysanthemum.

n2.speaker: Dolores
n2.text: Thank you. Some things are better left as they are. It is a great mercy. People forget that, how kind it is, to leave things as they are.

n3.speaker: Dolores
n3.aside: She is humming it too. She doesn't know. Her face has gone the colour of the candles.

end.text: She waves at the Chapel window, the lake on the other side of it, with great formality, like a woman waving off a train she is afraid to board.

n0.speaker: Silas
n0.text: Evening, Vern. I've a dedication, if you've the room. 'For the man by the water.' No song. You choose.
n0.aside: Three watches on his wrist. Three times. None of them tonight's.

choices.text: "Who is the man by the water, Silas?"

n1.speaker: Silas
n1.text: He's a clockmaker. He isn't from around here. ...He's from rather nearer than that.

n2.speaker: Silas
n2.text: You're a kind man, Vernon. Mind how you play the thing you're thinking of playing. If you do.

n3.speaker: Silas
n3.text: If it goes out tonight, a good many people in this valley will sit down very suddenly in their kitchens. Play it softly. They'll need time to remember.

choices.text: (Nod. It's a threat and a gift.)

end.text: Silas does not wave at the lake. He taps the glass of the middle watch with one finger, three times, as if tapping on a door.
